description: Create 7 new game screens under src/features/game/. All screens use the game dark theme tokens (game.bg, game.purple etc.) and Space+ CSS utilities. Each is a self-contained functional component with named export. No simulation/ changes. No existing screens touched.
steps: Step 1 — src/features/game/CampaignMapScreen.tsx: 8-level interactive mission map. Dark background (className='game-bg min-h-screen'). Header: Space+ AppShell variant='light' is NOT used here — wrap in a plain div with game-bg + star-field overlay for immersive feel. Top bar: back arrow (navigate('/missions')), title 'Campaign', XP counter from useMissionProgressStore. Main content: vertical or grid layout of 8 MissionNode cards. MissionNode: shows level number (large, gold if unlocked/completed, gray if locked), mission title, planet badge (moon/mars emoji), difficulty label, completion stars if done, lock icon if locked. A teal glowing connection line SVG between adjacent nodes. Active node pulses with pulse-level-node animation. Clicking an active node navigates to '/game/cinematic/:missionId'. Clicking a completed node navigates to '/game/cinematic/:missionId' (replay allowed). Data comes from MISSIONS (from @data/missions/mission-definitions) + useMissionProgressStore getMissionStatus. Props interface: CampaignMapScreenProps (empty). Export: export function CampaignMapScreen().

Step 2 — src/features/game/CinematicIntroScreen.tsx: Story intro screen shown before gameplay. Dark full-screen with planet orb CSS animation. Receives missionId from useParams() (react-router-dom). Finds mission from getMissionById(missionId). Shows: planet CSS orb (.moon-planet / .mars-planet / .purple-planet based on mission.bgTheme), mission number badge (gold), mission title (large white text, font-display2), story intro text (mission.storyIntro ?? mission.description) with typewriter effect (useEffect + useState to reveal characters ~40ms/char, skip if prefers-reduced-motion). Concept taught badge: 'You will learn: {mission.conceptTaught}'. Two buttons: 'Begin Mission' (game-btn-primary → navigate('/game/play/:missionId')), 'Skip Intro' (text button, same target). Props: CinematicIntroScreenProps (empty — reads from URL params). Export: export function CinematicIntroScreen().

Step 3 — src/features/game/GameplayScreen.tsx: The 2.5D interactive gameplay screen. This is the heart of the feature. Structure: (a) game-bg full screen, star-field overlay; (b) top HUD bar (fixed): mission day counter, resource mini-bars (O2/water/food/energy as thin colored bars with icon+value), pause button, 'Advance Day' button; (c) interactive room area (main content): CSS grid of 2–3 'rooms' — e.g. 'Command Center', 'Life Support Bay', 'Agriculture Module'. Each room is a game-card with a room illustration (CSS gradient + emoji icon), room name, status indicator (green/amber/red based on relevant resource), and hover state with cursor-pointer. Clicking a room triggers 'inspect' interaction (shows a side panel with room details, current status, and a tip from Astro-AI). (d) Event alert: if activeEventIds.length > 0, show a pulsing red banner 'ALERT: {event title}' with 'Respond Now' button that navigates to '/game/event/:missionId/:eventId'. (e) Right sidebar: current mission tasks checklist (from mission definition), Astro-AI hint panel (static tip based on planet type and day). (f) Bottom action bar: 'Advance Day' primary button, 'Emergency Ration' button (calls emergencyRation() from useMissionControl), 'End Mission' ghost button. Uses useMissionControl() hook for all simulation state. Uses useMissionProgressStore for current mission + task progress. On missionOutcome === 'success': navigate('/game/level-complete/:missionId'). On missionOutcome === 'failure': navigate('/game/game-over'). Receives missionId from useParams(). Calls initializeMission() in useEffect on mount if !missionStarted. Split into sub-components: HudBar, RoomGrid, RoomCard, EventAlertBanner, SidePanel, BottomActionBar — all in the same file (file will approach 300 lines; split RoomCard into a separate file src/features/game/RoomCard.tsx if needed). Props: GameplayScreenProps (empty). Export: export function GameplayScreen().

Step 4 — src/features/game/RoomCard.tsx: Extracted sub-component for interactive room cards used by GameplayScreen. Interface RoomCardProps: { readonly roomId: string, readonly name: string, readonly icon: string, readonly statusColor: 'good' | 'warn' | 'crit' | 'neutral', readonly isSelected: boolean, readonly onClick: () => void }. Renders a button (for keyboard accessibility) with game-card styling + status indicator dot + emoji icon + room name + subtle animation on hover. Export: export function RoomCard().

Step 5 — src/features/game/GameEventModal.tsx: Full-screen decision modal for event resolution. Displayed as a fixed overlay (z-50) with dark semi-transparent backdrop. Receives eventId and missionId from useParams(). Looks up the event from LUNAR_EVENTS / MARTIAN_EVENTS (import both, find by id). Shows: event title (large, red/amber warning text), event description (age-appropriate), affected systems badges, 2–3 choice cards with label + description + consequence preview. On choice selection: calls resolveEvent(eventId, choiceId) from useMissionControl(), shows consequence text for 1.5s, then navigates back to '/game/play/:missionId'. 'Consult Astro-AI' button: toggles a teal info box with the event's scientificExplanation (simplified for ages 8-12 — just show the event's scientificExplanation field). Props: GameEventModalProps (empty — reads from URL). Export: export function GameEventModal().

Step 6 — src/features/game/PauseMenuOverlay.tsx: Pause/settings overlay. Fixed full-screen overlay (z-50, dark bg-black/70 backdrop). Triggered by the pause button in GameplayScreen HUD or keyboard Escape key. Since this is a separate route ('/game/pause'), GameplayScreen navigates to it and the overlay appears over the preserved game state. Menu items: 'Resume' (game-btn-teal, navigate back with useNavigate(-1)), 'Restart Mission' (secondary, navigate to '/game/cinematic/:missionId'), 'Main Menu' (ghost, navigate to '/missions'), 'Settings' sub-panel toggle (shows volume slider for audioManager.setVolume(), mute toggle). Also displays: current mission day, current mission title, crew size. Accessible: role='dialog', aria-modal='true', aria-label='Pause menu', traps focus. Props: PauseMenuOverlayProps (empty — reads URL param). Export: export function PauseMenuOverlay().

Step 7 — src/features/game/LevelCompleteScreen.tsx: Level completion celebration screen. Dark bg with gold particle effect (CSS radial-gradient dots + float-astronaut animation on an astronaut emoji). Shows: mission title, 'Mission Complete!' heading (.gold-glow-text), earned stars (1–3 large amber star icons from @phosphor-icons/react), XP earned (calculated: starsEarned * 20 + mission.number * 10), concept taught badge, story outro text (mission.storyOutro ?? 'Great work, Commander!'). Task summary: checklist of completed tasks. Two buttons: 'Continue Campaign' (game-btn-primary → useMissionProgressStore.completeMission(missionId, starsEarned), navigate to '/game/campaign')), 'View Full Report' (game-btn-teal → navigate to '/debrief')). Receives missionId from useParams(). Derives starsEarned from missionScore (from useMissionStore) using same formula as MissionControlScreen: max(1, min(3, ceil(currentMissionDay/totalDays*3))). Props: LevelCompleteScreenProps (empty). Export: export function LevelCompleteScreen().

Step 8 — src/features/game/GameOverScreen.tsx: Game failure screen. Dark bg with red tint overlay (rgba(239,68,68,0.08) background). Shows: '💔' emoji large, 'Mission Failed' heading (text-game-red), failure reason (derive from activeFaultStates array in useMissionStore: OXYGEN_DEPLETED → 'Your crew ran out of oxygen', WATER_DEPLETED → 'Your crew ran out of water', FOOD_DEPLETED → 'Your crew ran out of food', POWER_CRITICAL → 'Power reached critical levels', RADIATION_CRITICAL → 'Radiation became critical', default → 'The mission could not be completed'), day reached ('You survived X days'), what went wrong (educational tip: 1 sentence per fault state explaining the science, pulled from a static map in this file). 1 star consolation award. Two buttons: 'Try Again' (game-btn-primary → navigate to '/game/cinematic/:missionId' using currentMissionId from useMissionProgressStore), 'Return to Campaign' (game-btn-teal → navigate to '/game/campaign')). Props: GameOverScreenProps (empty). Export: export function GameOverScreen().
acceptance_criteria: src/features/game/ directory contains: CampaignMapScreen.tsx, CinematicIntroScreen.tsx, GameplayScreen.tsx, RoomCard.tsx, GameEventModal.tsx, PauseMenuOverlay.tsx, LevelCompleteScreen.tsx, GameOverScreen.tsx
All 8 files have named exports (e.g. export function CampaignMapScreen())
No src/simulation/ imports in any game screen
CampaignMapScreen renders 8 mission nodes using MISSIONS array
GameplayScreen uses useMissionControl() for all simulation state
npx vitest run shows 219 passing (no regressions — new tests in FEAT-003)
findings: All 8 steps implemented successfully. Build passes (16.09s, 44 chunks). Tests: 223 passing (no regressions — FEAT-002 adds no new tests per spec; tests are in FEAT-003). Files created: CampaignMapScreen.tsx (8-node map with moon/mars/expert chapters, teal connectors, pulse animation), CinematicIntroScreen.tsx (typewriter effect, prefers-reduced-motion respected, planet orb float), GameplayScreen.tsx (HUD with mini resource bars, 3-room grid, side panel, event alert banner, bottom action bar), RoomCard.tsx (extracted sub-component, keyboard-accessible button), GameEventModal.tsx (full-screen overlay, choice cards, Astro-AI consult toggle, 1.5s consequence then navigate), PauseMenuOverlay.tsx (Escape key + focus trap, volume slider, mute toggle, settings sub-panel), LevelCompleteScreen.tsx (gold particles, star rating, XP summary, task checklist, story outro), GameOverScreen.tsx (fault-state-derived failure reason, 1-star consolation, educational tips). Router updated with 7 new /game/* routes. One fix needed: initialResources not exposed by useMissionControl — read from useMissionStore directly in GameplayScreen.
